industry.cleanAir: Exhaust after-treatment content is set by emission law: BS-VI (Apr-2020) multiplied content per vehicle; BS-VI stage 2 (RDE) followed in 2023. Next: CAFE-3 fuel-economy norms for cars expected in 2027 (gasoline direct injection needs particulate filters from 2027, per management), TREM-V for tractors and BS-VII (not notified by 30-Sep-2026). Management sizes CAFE-3 + BS-VII at Rs1,300-1,400 cr of extra industry content. JM Financial (Jan-2026): PV clean-air market Rs4,650-5,100 cr by FY30 (6-8% CAGR), CV/off-highway 13-15% CAGR; CAFE adds Rs1,000-1,500 per car, BS-VII ~Rs2,000 per truck.
industry.ride: Shock absorbers and struts go into every vehicle, ICE or electric. Premiumisation (UVs 34.6% of PV volume in FY20, 65.4% in FY25, JM Financial) and EVs (heavier, low centre of gravity) push buyers towards passive-plus (DCx, ~2x conventional content) and semi-active (~4x) dampers. Domestic PV OE suspension market +8-10% CAGR FY25-30 (CRISIL via JM).
industry.cycle: Served market (PV+CV, company) grew 16.2% in Q1FY27 on the Sep-2025 GST cut for small cars and a CV upcycle; the West Asia war lifted crude-linked input costs from Mar-2026.
industry.evRisk: Battery EVs carry no exhaust: about 20% of VAR (PV clean air) is exposed to full EV adoption (JM Financial); hybrids, CNG and flex-fuel keep or raise content.

peers.note: The auto-component set used in the Bosch, Motherson, Uno Minda, Endurance, MSWIL and ZF CV initiations, with TENNIND itself excluded (PLAYBOOK §7c). No listed Indian pure-play exhaust peer has Screener data in the library (Sharda Motor is not on file).

Risks: EV shift (~20% of VAR), norm delays, reliance on parent technology and royalty.

moat.text: Thousands of Tenneco patents and global platforms (Euro VII PoC, semi-active dampers, GPF) for a 2.5% royalty; India-developed DCx/MARD show some local capability.
Exhaust and dampers are validated per platform for 5-7 year programme lives; 17-29 year relationships with the top five OEMs.
#1 in CV clean air (58%), off-highway (68%) and PV shocks (55%).
18-19% EBITDA on VAR and ~94% ROCE (company) say it is efficient, but substrates and steel are passed through: the margin is on conversion only.
Clean-air content falls to zero in battery EVs (~20% of VAR in PV clean air); the parent decides which export programmes India gets.

critiques: Clean Air grew only 5.5% in FY26 and 9.6% in Q1FY27 against a 16% served market: absent at the largest PV maker and in EVs.
Margins fell 170 bp YoY on VAR in Q1FY27; listing costs and non-indexed inputs are not fully recovered.
Royalty is charged on revenue including pass-through substrates, so rising precious-metal prices raise the royalty with no extra value added.
The parent sold 15% within nine months of the IPO; another sale is possible once the 90-day lock-up ends.
~70% of the export order book is Tenneco-to-Tenneco: export growth depends on the parent's allocation and transfer prices.
